title: Daily arXiv physics shortlist — announcement batch 13 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred notable-paper ranking, not a readership or download ranking, and citation evidence is sparse—Semantic Scholar listed zero citations for all eight selected papers at the 2026-11-15 01:45:42 UTC snapshot.

sections.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
sections.abstract: The authors derive a three-time witness for quantum memory that pairwise tests can miss and demonstrate the hierarchy in a time-continuous superconducting-qubit experiment.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report a three-time witness value W3=-0.24±0.03 in their transmon experiment, while numerical pairwise models remain classical over the tested observation window.
sections.evidence_type: experimental and theoretical; an analytic qubit-channel witness and channel tomography on two superconducting transmons with time-independent couplings
sections.unique_caveat: The witness is derived for qubits, and the claim that every pair admits a classical explanation relies on numerical optimization; the multi-time signature also depends on the observation window and drive regime.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A specialist Quantum Research Center explainer discusses the result; the paper couples a new analytic witness to a superconducting-qubit demonstration, making it one of the batch’s clearest theory-plus-experiment results.

sections.title: JWST Rocky Worlds DDT Observations of LTT 1445 A b and c in Secondary Eclipse Using MIRI/F1500W
sections.abstract: Three JWST/MIRI eclipse visits, combined with earlier spectra and radial velocities, indicate that nearby rocky planet LTT 1445 A b has no substantial atmosphere, while its sibling planet c remains weakly constrained.
sections.claimed_result: For planet b, the authors infer a CO2 partial pressure below 0.6 mbar and surface pressure of roughly 0.1 bar or less; for c, they exclude only thick CO2-bearing atmospheres.
sections.evidence_type: observational; JWST MIRI/F1500W secondary eclipses of both planets across three visits, prior JWST spectra, and a joint fit including 220 radial velocities
sections.unique_caveat: Planet c’s potentially grazing eclipse and overlapping events leave its eclipse depth poorly constrained; planet b’s atmospheric limits depend on retrieval and forward-model assumptions, and do not exclude every thin non-CO2 atmosphere.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors compare three independent data reductions and a joint fit; the study also received science-media coverage and a paper-focused research summary.

sections.title: Observation of the $\Lambda(1520)$ suppression in Pb-Pb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{\rm NN}} = 5.02$ TeV
sections.abstract: ALICE measures a central-to-peripheral reduction of the Λ(1520)/Λ yield ratio in 5.02 TeV Pb-Pb collisions and compares the trend with hadronization and transport models.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration measures a central-to-peripheral suppression of 0.589±0.015 stat±0.086 syst and finds that MUSIC coupled to the SMASH hadronic afterburner reproduces the centrality trend within uncertainties.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ALICE Pb-Pb collision data at sqrt(sNN)=5.02 TeV, compared with statistical-hadronization and hydrodynamic-plus-transport calculations
sections.unique_caveat: The systematic uncertainty is material, and the model comparison supports late-stage hadronic effects without uniquely separating rescattering from regeneration.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: ALICE reports a 6.8-sigma significance across six centrality classes, calls this the first above-5-sigma observation of resonance suppression within one collision system, and notes submission to PRL.

sections.title: New measurement of BR$(K^+\rightarrow\pi^+\nu\bar\nu)$ at the NA62 experiment
authors: Silvia Martellotti on behalf of NA62 Collaboration
sections.abstract: NA62 presents a new K+→π+νν-bar branching-ratio measurement using its 2023–2024 data, which doubles the effective sample and improves sensitivity to this rare decay.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration reports a branching ratio of 9.6(+1.9/-1.8)×10^-11, compatible with Standard Model predictions.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; NA62 kaon-decay data collected at CERN during 2016–2024, with the new 2023–2024 sample added to the analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The measurement’s relative uncertainty is about 20%; the authors state that 2026 data taking and analysis of the full dataset are ongoing, so it does not establish a deviation from the Standard Model.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The full paper reports a new result from the enlarged 2016–2024 NA62 sample for an exceptionally rare Standard-Model decay, with 20% relative uncertainty; the 2023–2024 addition doubles the effective sample size.

sections.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
sections.abstract: Mid-infrared pumping of NiO produces a finite-momentum two-magnon signal whose decay is much slower than previously reported two-magnon coherence times.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure a pump-induced bimagnon signal that peaks about 4 ps after excitation and decays with a fitted time constant of 28±11 ps.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; mid-infrared pumping and time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering at finite momentum at LCLS-II
sections.unique_caveat: The authors’ explanation of delayed growth as momentum redistribution is an interpretation, not a direct measurement of that redistribution; the decay estimate comes from a single-exponential fit with a stated 1-sigma covariance error.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper cross-lists four physics subfields and reports time-resolved RIXS evidence for a quantitative, long-lived driven excitation, linking magnetic materials, optical pumping, and quantum dynamics.

sections.title: The full Gaia colour-magnitude diagram with white dwarfs reveals a declining Milky Way star formation history
sections.abstract: A self-consistent population-synthesis fit to Gaia DR3 main-sequence and white-dwarf stars favors an early-peaking, subsequently declining Milky Way star-formation history with two later bursts.
sections.claimed_result: CALOMERA reproduces counts in each colour-magnitude region to within 3% and recovers two recent star-formation bursts near 2.4 and 0.5 Gyr ago.
sections.evidence_type: computational and observational; a semi-analytic chemo-dynamical population model calibrated against Gaia DR3 and three white-dwarf cooling libraries
sections.unique_caveat: The history is inferred under stellar-evolution, metallicity, and cooling assumptions; the authors find cooling-library differences concentrated among faint white dwarfs (MG greater than about 15).
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The authors fit 7.98 million Gaia DR3 stars, including about 110,000 white dwarfs, with 18 model parameters; the paper is submitted to MNRAS and uses three cooling libraries as a cross-check.

sections.title: Euclid Data Release 1 (DR1): The Euclid surveys at DR1
sections.abstract: This Euclid Collaboration paper describes the scope, implementation, and operational products of the mission’s DR1 surveys, including the Wide, Deep, auxiliary, calibration, and other fields.
sections.claimed_result: The collaboration describes survey operations and reports the Wide Survey coverage and validated area at DR1, alongside data from several additional Euclid fields.
sections.evidence_type: observational and data-release documentation; Euclid visible and near-infrared imaging and spectroscopy across multiple survey components
sections.unique_caveat: The 2,100 square-degree coverage is not all validated for higher-level science processing; this paper documents the release and operations rather than presenting an independent cosmological constraint.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: This is a mission-wide release overview for a major survey program; its checkable scale is 2,100 square degrees covered by the Wide Survey at DR1, of which 1,900 square degrees is validated in higher-level processing. The paper is intended for the Euclid DR1 A&A special issue.

sections.title: Lurkers at the Threshold: GWTC-4.0's near-threshold events
sections.abstract: The authors analyze 42 near-threshold GWTC-4.0 candidate signals using public strain data and obtain validated posterior results for 29, while flagging others as noise-affected or uninterpretable.
sections.claimed_result: The authors identify a possible neutron-star–black-hole merger candidate and two candidates with evidence for non-zero effective spin, while noting that further analysis is needed to establish robustness.
sections.evidence_type: observational reanalysis and computational; public gravitational-wave strain data and catalogue-style parameter estimation with automated posterior validation
sections.unique_caveat: These are marginal signals; several candidates are noise-affected or uninterpretable, and spin constraints are generally weak.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The work provides a reproducible, catalogue-style reanalysis of public GWTC-4.0 strain, posterior samples for 29 candidates, automated validation, and a compatible data release.
